evidence.observation: The MetadataClient class and its constructor. Given a MetadataClientConfig it validates apiKey/serviceId and constructs a V3HttpTransport (lines 124-131), so every /v3/meta/* and /v3/knowledge/* call routes through the transport's normalization instead of returning a raw response; given a duck-typed Transport (`"post" in configOrTransport`, line 118) it uses it as the injectable seam used by this contract demo. Missing credentials fail with a typed ParamError (lines 122-123) before any request is sent.

body() rejects a non-object request payload with a typed ParamError ("request payload must be an object", line 82) and strips undefined fields before dispatch. It is the shared guard for createUser/getUser/verifyAuth-style metadata calls, so a malformed client-side payload produces a typed client error rather than a raw server response.

requireAnyString() is the cross-field selector guard used by listTeams and listTasks. If none of the candidate fields is a non-empty string it throws a typed ParamError naming the operation and the required alternatives (line 93), i.e. a normalized client-side failure instead of a raw server error envelope.

getUserKey() is the representative one-line management-plane call (`POST /v3/meta/user-key/get`) used by the contract demo's primary failure case. Its return type Promise<UserKeyPublic> is satisfied only by the normalized envelope.data, and a non-zero business code rejects with the transport's typed TDAMError.

The listTasks overloads and implementation; line 224 calls requireAnyString(payload, ["team_id", "creator_user_id", "creator_user_key"], "listTasks"), so calling listTasks({}) fails as a typed ParamError before dispatch. This is the demo's client-side-failure case for the metadata client.

V3HttpTransport.request is where a metadata client's raw HTTP exchange is normalized. It raises TDAMError when the body is not JSON (line 90), when HTTP is non-ok or the envelope business code is non-zero (line 104) using numeric code plus request_id, and it returns only envelope.data merged with trace_id on success (lines 112-119). The thrown value is a typed error, never the parsed {code,message,request_id,data} envelope.

TDAMError is the normalized failure type: readonly code: number (line 13), readonly requestId: string (line 14) and optional structured details (line 24), with a formatted message. MetadataClient failures surface as this type, giving callers a stable typed shape instead of the raw response envelope. ParamError (line 5) is its TypeError-based sibling for client-side argument failures.

claims.claim: Because MetadataClient(config) builds a V3HttpTransport, any server failure on a metadata management call (/v3/meta/* or /v3/knowledge/*) is surfaced as a typed/normalized TDAMError exposing a numeric .code, string .requestId and structured .details; the raw response envelope shape {code,message,request_id,data} is never the thrown value.

A business error code inside an HTTP 200 envelope (e.g. code 40901) rejects as TDAMError with err.code === 40901 and err.details === envelope.data, while raw keys request_id/data are absent from the error object (only the normalized requestId/details accessors exist); when no trace header is present the request id falls back to envelope.request_id.

Client-side argument failures raised by MetadataClient are typed ParamError instances (a TypeError subclass): missing apiKey/serviceId in the constructor (lines 122-123), a non-object payload via body(), and listTasks({}) without any of team_id/creator_user_id/creator_user_key via requireAnyString (line 224) all throw before dispatch instead of leaking a raw response shape.

On success MetadataClient methods resolve to the normalized operation result: only envelope.data (plus trace_id) is returned, so getUserKey returns Promise<UserKeyPublic> and envelope keys code/message/request_id are not leaked onto the resolved object.

The normalization contract is proven by an executable, dependency-free demo (.prale-eval/demo/metadata-failure-contract.mjs) that loads the unmodified metadata-client.ts, drives it with a stubbed fetch, and asserts 10/10 cases pass, covering business-code errors, HTTP-status errors, non-JSON bodies, constructor/payload/selector ParamErrors, and the normalized success result.

conclusion: The metadata management client does not leak raw response shapes. Failures are normalized twice over: client-side validation failures (constructor credentials, non-object payloads, missing list selectors) throw the typed ParamError (a TypeError subclass), and every server-side failure observed on the wire (non-zero business code inside an HTTP 200 envelope, non-OK HTTP status, or a non-JSON body) is converted by V3HttpTransport.request into a typed TDAMError carrying a numeric code, a string requestId and optional structured details. Successful calls resolve to the envelope's data sub-object only (plus trace_id); the raw {code,message,request_id,data} envelope is neither returned nor thrown. This is demonstrated by the executable contract .prale-eval/demo/metadata-failure-contract.mjs, which loads the unmodified sdk/memory-core/typescript/src/v3/metadata-client.ts and passes 10/10 assertions. One residual boundary is recorded rather than claimed: a malformed success envelope (code 0 with non-object data) is passed through unchanged because the transport asserts only envelope parseability, not that data is an object.
